name: The Original Dawn Redwood of the Arboretum
age_estimate: roughly 77 years, grown from seed collected in Hubei, China in 1948

location.address: Arnold Arboretum of Harvard University, near the Hunnewell Visitor Center, opposite the Arborway Gate

access: Free, public arboretum, open dawn to dusk
transport: Forest Hills MBTA station (Orange Line), roughly 20 minute walk to the Arborway Gate and Hunnewell Visitor Center, or the 39 bus to the Arborway stop
verify_notes: Accession 524-48*AA, Metasequoia glyptostroboides. Grown from seed in the 1948 collection sent from Hubei Province, China by forester Zhan Wang / botanist Hu Xiansu, the material that reached the Arnold Arboretum within months of the species' 1946 rediscovery as a living tree rather than a fossil (it had been known only from fossils dated tens of millions of years old). Arboretum copy calls this seed lot's trees 'the first of its kind to grow in North America in over two million years.' The same 1948 shipment is the origin point of the whole Metasequoia introduction to the West, so this specific tree predates and directly precedes the Public Garden's 1963-planted dawn redwood (bos_004) by 15 years: same species, same seed source, one generation earlier, joins the same story if the writer wants to link them. A second, separately numbered 1948 accession (3-48*A) is referred to elsewhere as 'the Arboretum's oldest dawn redwood... visited along Conifer Path'; I could not resolve in this pass whether 3-48*A and 524-48*AA are the same individual under different labels or two separate survivors of the same 1948 seed lot, so verify_notes flags this rather than picking one silently. Both sources used are Arnold Arboretum's own site (different articles/pages), so this counts as single-institution sourcing, consistent with how bos_002 and bos_003 were flagged for the same reason. No individual tree-level coordinates are published; the pin is the Visitor Center area, which the Arboretum's own copy places the accession near. Note for the writer: a possible discrepancy was found in the FoPG dawn redwood article used for bos_004, which describes an 'older sibling' dawn redwood planted 1963 standing across the path from the Charles/Beacon specimen already published as bos_004 (bos_004's own text says IT was planted 1963 at Charles/Beacon) -- worth a look before publishing, not something this pass touched or resolved.

name: The Wilson Paperbark Maple
age_estimate: roughly 119 years (collected as a wild seedling in 1907)

location.address: Arnold Arboretum of Harvard University, Maple Collection, off Meadow Road
location.neighbourhood: Meadow Road, Arnold Arboretum, Jamaica Plain

access: Free, public arboretum, open dawn to dusk
transport: Forest Hills MBTA station (Orange Line), roughly 10-12 minute walk via the Forest Hills Gate and Meadow Road
verify_notes: Accession 12488*B. Plant explorer Ernest Henry Wilson dug two seedlings of Acer griseum from a woodland north of Yichang, Hubei Province, China in autumn 1907 and shipped them to the Arnold Arboretum; both survived and are described by the Arboretum as the first and oldest paperbark maples on the North American continent, the genetic source of most paperbark maples later planted in the US. The species is now endangered in the wild in China, so this is ex-situ conservation as much as a garden specimen. Visually distinctive: luminous, exfoliating cinnamon-copper bark, especially striking in winter sun, which is also its best_time case (bare-season structure/bark rather than flower or fall colour). Second source is Google Arts & Culture's own feature on the introduction (an independent publication, though its content derives from the Arboretum's history, so treat this as corroboration rather than a fully independent second source; both Arboretum pages used are also same-institution). No individual tree-level coordinates published; pinned to the Maple Collection area off Meadow Road, 5-8 minutes' walk from Forest Hills Gate per the Arboretum's own directions page. A second historic 1907 Wilson seedling reportedly also survives nearby per the same sources; not separately verified or pinned this pass, left as an implicit twin at the same spot rather than a second entry.
